<article class="devsite-article">
  
  
  
    <div class="devsite-banner devsite-banner-announcement nocontent" data-nosnippet
      
        
    background="orange"
  
      >
      <div class="devsite-banner-message">
        <div class="devsite-banner-message-text">
          <p><strong>Firebase Studio is sunsetting on March 22, 2027.</strong> As of June 22, 2026, new workspace creation and user signup are disabled. You can continue to work in and migrate your existing workspaces to Google AI Studio or Google Antigravity. <a href="/docs/studio/migrating-project">Learn how to migrate.</a></p> <p><em>Any apps already deployed to Firebase will continue to run even after the sunset date. Also, all our <u>core Firebase products</u> (like Firestore, Authentication, App Hosting, etc.) are <u>not impacted</u> by the Firebase Studio sunset.</em></p>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  
  
  

  <div class="devsite-article-meta nocontent" role="navigation" data-nosnippet>
    
    
    <ul class="devsite-breadcrumb-list"
  
    aria-label="Breadcrumb">
  
  <li class="devsite-breadcrumb-item
             ">
    
    
    
      
        
  <a href="https://firebase.google.com/"
      
        class="devsite-breadcrumb-link gc-analytics-event"
      
        data-category="Site-Wide Custom Events"
      
        data-label="Breadcrumbs"
      
        data-value="1"
      
        track-type="globalNav"
      
        track-name="breadcrumb"
      
        track-metadata-position="1"
      
        track-metadata-eventdetail="Firebase"

<aside class="tip"><strong>Tip:</strong><span> If you don&#39;t find an answer to your question, contact
  <a href="https://firebase.google.com/support/troubleshooter/studio">Firebase Support</a>
  or <a href="https://community.firebasestudio.dev/" class="external">ask in our community forums</a>.</span></aside>
<h2 id="general-faqs" data-text="Firebase Studio general" tabindex="-1"><span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> general</h2>

<h3 id="download-files" data-text="How do I download my files from Firebase Studio?" tabindex="-1">How do I download my files from
<span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span>?</h3>

<p>To download your files as a zip file:</p>

<ul>
<li>Right-click on any directory in the Explorer pane and select
<strong>Zip and Download</strong>.</li>
</ul>

<p>To download everything in your project directory:</p>

<ol>
<li><p>Select <strong>File &gt; Open Folder</strong>.</p></li>
<li><p>Accept the default <code translate="no" dir="ltr">/home/user</code> directory.</p></li>
<li><p>After the files load, right-click your working directory and select
<strong>Zip and Download</strong>. If using
the <span class="notranslate">App Prototyping agent</span>, your working directory will be <code translate="no" dir="ltr">studio</code>. If
using a template or uploaded project, this will be your project name.</p></li>
<li><p>When prompted to rebuild the environment, click <strong>Cancel</strong>.</p></li>
<li><p>After your download completes, re-open your working directory from the
<strong>File</strong> menu to move back into your workspace.</p></li>
</ol>
<aside class="tip"><strong>Tip:</strong><span> You can also <a href="/docs/studio/github">export to GitHub</a>.</span></aside>
<h3 id="third-party-cookies" data-text="Third-party cookies aren't enabled." tabindex="-1">Third-party cookies aren't enabled.</h3>

<p>Before you get started, you might need to enable third-party cookies for your
browser. <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> requires third-party cookies in most browsers
to authenticate workspaces.</p>
<div><devsite-selector data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="chrome" data-text="Chrome" tabindex="-1">Chrome</h3><p>On desktop:</p>

<ol>
<li>Open <strong>Settings</strong>.</li>
<li>Open the <strong>Privacy and Security</strong> tab.</li>
<li>Make sure <strong>Allow all cookies</strong> is enabled.</li>
<li>Open <a href="https://studio.firebase.google.com/" class="external"><span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span></a>.</li>
<li>Click the visibility icon in the address bar <span
class="material-icons" aria-hidden="true" translate="no">visibility_off</span> to open the <strong>Tracking
Protection</strong> panel. Turn on the <strong>Third-party cookies</strong> setting to
temporarily allow third-party cookies. This enables cookies on
<span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> for 90 days.</li>
</ol>

<p>On Android phones and tablets:</p>

<ol>
<li>Tap (<span class="material-icons" aria-hidden="true" translate="no">more_vert</span>) <strong>More</strong> &gt;
<strong>Settings</strong>.</li>
<li>Open <strong>Site settings</strong> &gt; <strong>Third-party cookies</strong>.</li>
<li>Make sure <strong>Allow all cookies</strong> is enabled.</li>
<li>Open <a href="https://studio.firebase.google.com/" class="external"><span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span></a>.</li>
<li>Click the visibility icon in the address bar <span
class="material-icons" aria-hidden="true" translate="no">visibility_off</span> to open the <strong>Tracking
Protection</strong> panel. Turn on the <strong>Third-party cookies</strong> setting to
temporarily allow third-party cookies. This enables cookies on
<span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> for 90 days.</li>
</ol>

<p>On iPhones and iPads:</p>

<ol>
<li>Open the <strong>Settings</strong> app &gt; <strong>Apps</strong> &gt; <strong>Chrome</strong>.</li>
<li>Turn on <strong>Allow Cross-Website Tracking</strong>.</li>
<li>Open <a href="https://studio.firebase.google.com/" class="external"><span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span></a>.</li>
</ol></section>
<section><h3 id="safari" data-text="Safari" tabindex="-1">Safari</h3><p>On desktop:</p>

<ol>
<li>Open <strong>Safari &gt; Settings...</strong>.</li>
<li>Turn off the following settings:
<ul>
<li><strong>Advanced &gt; Block all cookies</strong></li>
<li><strong>Privacy &gt; Prevent cross-site tracking</strong></li>
</ul></li>
<li>Open <a href="https://studio.firebase.google.com/" class="external"><span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span></a>.</li>
</ol>

<p>On iPhones and iPads:</p>

<ol>
<li>Open the <strong>Settings</strong> app &gt; <strong>Apps</strong> &gt; <strong>Safari</strong>.</li>
<li>Turn off the following settings:
<ul>
<li><strong>Prevent Cross-Site Tracking</strong></li>
<li><strong>Advanced</strong> &gt; <strong>Block All Cookies</strong></li>
</ul></li>
<li>Open <a href="https://studio.firebase.google.com/" class="external"><span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span></a>.</li>
</ol></section>
<section><h3 id="firefox" data-text="Firefox" tabindex="-1">Firefox</h3><p>You don&#39;t need to enable third-party cookies for Firefox.
Open <a href="https://studio.firebase.google.com/" class="external"><span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span></a>.</p></section>
<section><h3 id="opera" data-text="Opera" tabindex="-1">Opera</h3><ol>
<li>Open Opera.</li>
<li>Open the menu and click <strong>Settings</strong>.</li>
<li>Go to the <strong>Privacy &amp; Security</strong> section and expand the
<strong>Third-party cookies</strong> option.</li>
<li>Select <strong>Block third-party cookies in Incognito mode</strong> or
<strong>Allow third-party cookies</strong>.</li>
<li>Open <a href="https://studio.firebase.google.com/" class="external"><span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span></a>.</li>
</ol></section>
<section><h3 id="arc" data-text="Arc" tabindex="-1">Arc</h3><ol>
<li>Go to <a href="arc://settings">arc://settings</a>.</li>
<li>Go to the <strong>Privacy and security</strong> section and expand the
<strong>Third-party cookies</strong> option.</li>
<li>Select <strong>Block third-party cookies in Incognito mode</strong> or
<strong>Allow third-party cookies</strong>.</li>
<li>Open <a href="https:https://studio.firebase.google.com/" class="external"><span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span></a>.</li>
</ol></section>
<section><h3 id="brave" data-text="Brave" tabindex="-1">Brave</h3><p>You don&#39;t need to enable third-party cookies for Brave. Open
<a href="https:https://studio.firebase.google.com/" class="external"><span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span></a>.</p></section>
</devsite-selector></div>
<p><section class="expandable" expanded id="3p-cookies"></p>

<h3 class="showalways" id="3p-cookies" data-text="Why does Firebase Studio need third-party (3P) cookies enabled?" tabindex="-1">Why does <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> need
third-party (3P) cookies enabled?</h3>

<p><span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> needs 3P cookies enabled since we render an iframe from
one domain (a subdomain of <code translate="no" dir="ltr">cloudworkstations.dev</code>) on another domain
(<code translate="no" dir="ltr">studio.firebase.google.com</code>), and 3P cookies enable secure cross-origin
communication.</p>

<p></section></p>

<p><section class="expandable" expanded id="service-accounts-in-workspace"></p>

<h3 class="showalways" id="service-accounts-in-workspace" data-text="Why do I see references to service accounts in my Firebase Studio workspace?" tabindex="-1">Why do I see
references to service accounts in my <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> workspace?</h3>

<p><span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> workspaces use service accounts to fetch the workstation
image as the workspace is created, and also for some minimal logging and metrics
to verify that the workstation starts successfully.</p>

<p>Some service accounts (such as those listed below) are used by multiple
workspaces, so you shouldn&#39;t grant these service accounts access to any
personal projects.</p>

<p>These service accounts are used by multiple workspaces:</p>

<ul>
<li><nobr><code translate="no" dir="ltr">id-monospace-workstations-sa@<var translate="no">PROJECT_ID</var>.iam.gserviceaccount.com</code></nobr></li>
<li><nobr><code translate="no" dir="ltr">monospace-trace-dev@<var translate="no">PROJECT_ID</var>.iam.gserviceaccount.com</code></nobr></li>
</ul>

<p></section></p>

<p><section class="expandable" expanded id="update-app"></p>

<h3 class="showalways" id="update-app" data-text="How do I update to the latest version of React or Next.js?" tabindex="-1">How do I update to the latest
version of React or Next.js?</h3>

<p>A critical Remote Code Execution (RCE) vulnerability affects applications built
with Next.js and React Server Components. To protect your application and data,
you must update to the latest stable version.</p>

<ol>
<li>Open your Firebase Studio project, and switch to
<img src="/static/docs/studio/images/icons/codicon-code.svg" alt="Code switch icon" class="inline-icon"> 
<span class="notranslate">Code</span> view.</li>
<li>Open the terminal (<code translate="no" dir="ltr">Shift+Ctrl+C</code>), and run the command
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">npx fix-react2shell-next</code>.</li>
<li>Follow the prompts in the terminal to proceed and apply any fixes.
<img src="/static/docs/studio/images/terminal-command-applied.png" alt="fixes applied"></li>
<li>When the process completes, <a href="/docs/studio/deploy-app">publish your updated app</a>.</li>
</ol>

<p></section></p>

<p><section class="expandable" expanded id="unable-to-forward-request"></p>

<h3 class="showalways" id="unable-to-forward-request" data-text="While opening a workspace, the message Unable to forward your request to backend. Couldn't connect to a server on port 80 appears." tabindex="-1">While opening a workspace,
the message <em>Unable to forward your request to backend. Couldn't
connect to a server on port 80</em> appears.</h3>

<p>Wait approximately five seconds and refresh the page.</p>

<p></section></p>

<p><section class="expandable" expanded id="resolve-bad-states"></p>

<h3 class="showalways" id="resolve-bad-states" data-text="My preview doesn't load, but I can't find any issues in code. How can I restart Firebase Studio?" tabindex="-1">My preview doesn't load, but I
can't find any issues in code. How can I restart <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span>?</h3>

<p>If <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> isn&#39;t refreshing properly (typically as a result of major
refactors, or changes to your environment <code translate="no" dir="ltr">dev.nix</code> file), open the command
palette
(<code translate="no" dir="ltr">Cmd+Shift+P</code> on Mac or <code translate="no" dir="ltr">Ctrl+Shift+P</code> on ChromeOS, Windows, or
Linux) and run the <strong>Hard Restart</strong> command. If that doesn&#39;t work,
try running the <strong>Rebuild Environment</strong> command.</p>

<p></section></p>

<p><section class="expandable" expanded id="unresponsive-workspace"></p>

<h3 class="showalways" id="unresponsive-workspace" data-text="My workspace is not responsive, all I see is a blank screen when it loads" tabindex="-1">My workspace is not
responsive, all I see is a blank screen when it loads</h3>

<p>If your workspace is not responding, you can try restarting the VM. To do this:</p>

<ol>
<li><p>From <a href="https://studio.firebase.google.com/"><span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span></a>, click the
<strong>More</strong> (<span class="material-icons" aria-hidden="true" translate="no">more_horiz</span>) menu,
then select <strong>Restart</strong>.</p></li>
<li><p>When prompted, click <strong>Restart</strong> again.</p></li>
<li><p>Re-open your workspace.</p></li>
</ol>

<p></section></p>

<p><section class="expandable" expanded id="spin-up-new-vm"></p>

<h3 class="showalways" id="spin-up-new-vm" data-text="While creating a workspace, I see a message, Whoops...We need to start a new VM, and the UI hangs after that." tabindex="-1">While creating a workspace, I see a
message, <em>Whoops...We need to start a new VM</em>, and the UI hangs after
that.</h3>

<p><span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> maintains a warm pool of VMs used to provision
workspaces on demand. When the pool runs low, the workspaces are
provisioned after a new virtual machine is started. The process can take
time (sometimes up to five minutes) but eventually succeeds.</p>

<p></section></p>

<p><section class="expandable" expanded id="no-space-home"></p>

<h3 class="showalways" id="no-space-home" data-text="[Errno 28] No space left on device" tabindex="-1">[Errno 28] No space left on
device</h3>

<p>You might encounter this message if the disk is full. The <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span>
workspace provides:</p>

<ul>
<li>100 GiB total disk space for <a href="/docs/studio/get-started-workspace#configure-nix-file">Nix
packages</a> and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">/tmp</code></li>
<li>10 GiB for your <code translate="no" dir="ltr">/home</code> directory</li>
</ul>

<p></section></p>

<p><section class="expandable" expanded id="internal-error-create-new-workspace"></p>

<h3 class="showalways" id="internal-error-create-new-workspace" data-text="When creating a workspace, I receive an internal error occurred." tabindex="-1">When
creating a workspace, I receive <em>an internal error occurred</em>.</h3>

<p>In most cases of internal errors during workspace provisioning, refreshing the
page after a minute or so should get you past the error and into the workspace.</p>

<p></section></p>

<p><section class="expandable" expanded id="workspace-limits"></p>

<h3 class="showalways" id="workspace-limits" data-text="How many workspaces can I create?" tabindex="-1">How many workspaces can I
create?</h3>

<p>The <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> no-cost plan is limited to three workspaces per user.
You can increase the number of workspaces you can create up to 10 by joining
the <a href="https://developers.google.com/profile/u/_/dashboard">Google Developer
Program</a>.
To upgrade to 30 workspaces, subscribe to the <a href="https://developers.google.com/profile/u/_/plans-and-pricing">Google Developer Premium
Program</a>.</p>

<p></section></p>

<p><section class="expandable" expanded id="submit-feature-request"></p>

<h3 class="showalways" id="submit-feature-request" data-text="How do I submit a feature request or feedback on an issue I encountered? " tabindex="-1">How do I submit a feature
request or feedback on an issue I encountered?
</h3>

<p>If you encounter an issue while using <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> or have a feature
request, <a href="https://firebase.google.com/support/troubleshooter/studio">contact Firebase
Support</a>.</p>

<p></section></p>

<p><section class="expandable" expanded id="feature-removed"></p>

<h3 class="showalways" id="feature-removed" data-text="I was using a particular feature in Firebase Studio but I can't find it anymore. Why was it removed? " tabindex="-1">I was using a particular feature in
<span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> but I can't find it anymore. Why was it removed?
</h3>

<p>Some of the features in <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> are experimental. We periodically
remove features that aren&#39;t living up to your expectations or our own.</p>

<p></section></p>

<h2 id="code-faqs" data-text="Firebase Studio Code workspaces" tabindex="-1"><span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> Code workspaces</h2>

<p><section class="expandable" expanded id="ide-load-emulator-blank"></p>

<h3 class="showalways" id="ide-load-emulator-blank" data-text="My workspace loads, but the emulator is blank." tabindex="-1">My workspace loads, but the
emulator is blank.</h3>

<p>We&#39;re actively improving the reliability of our cloud-based emulators. If a page
refresh does not fix the problem, <a href="/support/troubleshooter/studio">report the issue to Firebase
Support</a>.</p>

<p></section></p>

<p><section class="expandable" expanded id="flutter-version"></p>

<h3 class="showalways" id="flutter-version" data-text="Firebase Studio workspaces have a Flutter version that is incompatible with my project." tabindex="-1"><span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> workspaces
have a Flutter version that is incompatible with my project.</h3>

<p>You can upgrade or downgrade the version of almost all pre-installed
software inside a workspace just as you would on your local machine (using
apt-get or brew). You can upgrade or downgrade software in your workspace,
but installed software is not persistent across sessions. We recommend
including all required packages in your
<a href="/docs/studio/customize-workspace">dev.nix</a> file.</p>

<p></section></p>



<p><section class="expandable" expanded id="broken-sharing"></p>

<h3 class="showalways" id="broken-sharing" data-text="I shared my workstation URL with someone, but they cannot see it." tabindex="-1">I shared my workstation URL with
someone, but they cannot see it.</h3>

<p>You can only share a workspace URL with users that have access to the workspace.
Users without permission see an error when trying to visit the URL. Be sure to
explicitly <a href="/docs/studio/share-your-workspace">share the workspace with them</a>.</p>

<p></section></p>

<p><section class="expandable" expanded id="sharing-visibility"></p>

<h3 class="showalways" id="sharing-visibility" data-text="When I share my workstation, what can my collaborator see?" tabindex="-1">When I share my workstation, what
can my collaborator see?</h3>

<p>Users added to your workspace have complete access to the VM&#39;s entire file
system, which may contain sensitive files like private keys and access
tokens that are stored on disk. <strong>Only share your workspace with
people you trust.</strong> While this approach helps other users view the exact
state of your workspace, it means that they see everything on your
workspace.</p>

<p></section></p>

<p><section class="expandable" expanded id="broken-sharing-publish-and-monitor"></p>

<h3 class="showalways" id="broken-sharing-publish-and-monitor" data-text="I shared my workspace; why can't my collaborator publish or monitor my app?" tabindex="-1">I shared my workspace;
why can't my collaborator publish or monitor my app?</h3>

<p>Users added to your workspace may not have permission to its underlying Firebase
project which powers the &quot;App overview&quot; publishing and monitoring features. To
grant them permission to your Firebase project, see <a href="/support/faq#projects-permissions-and-access">Permissions and access to
Firebase
projects</a></p>

<p></section></p>

<p><section class="expandable" expanded id="custom-frameworks"></p>

<h3 class="showalways" id="custom-frameworks" data-text="Can I use frameworks that Firebase Studio does not have a template for to build my application?" tabindex="-1">Can I use frameworks that
<span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> does not have a template for to build my application?</h3>

<p>Yes! You can <a href="/docs/studio/customize-workspace">customize your environment</a> to
work with just about any framework or language in <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span>.</p>

<p></section></p>

<p><section class="expandable" expanded id="flutter-deploy"></p>

<h3 class="showalways" id="flutter-deploy" data-text="What target directory should I select when publishing a Flutter app to Firebase Hosting?" tabindex="-1">What target directory should I
select when publishing a Flutter app to <span class="notranslate">Firebase Hosting</span>?</h3>

<p>Choose the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">build/web</code> directory. This directory should contain an <code translate="no" dir="ltr">index.html</code>
and all the static assets needed to render your web app after the app is built
successfully (via <code translate="no" dir="ltr">flutter build web</code>).</p>

<p></section></p>

<p><section class="expandable" expanded id="app-backend"></p>

<h3 class="showalways" id="app-backend" data-text="How can I set up my app's backend on my workspace so that my frontend can communicate with it?" tabindex="-1">How can I set up my app's backend
on my workspace so that my frontend can communicate with it?</h3>

<p>You can temporarily publicly open the TCP port your backend server is running on
to make it easier to develop your frontend and backend separately, across
different workspaces:</p>

<ol>
<li><p>Start your backend or API server either manually in a terminal, or as part
of your <a href="/docs/studio/customize-workspace"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">dev.nix</code> file</a>&#39;s preview
configuration or <code translate="no" dir="ltr">onStart</code> lifecycle hook.</p></li>
<li><p>Click the <strong><span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span></strong> icon in the activity bar (on the left by
default) to open the <strong><span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span></strong> panel.</p></li>
<li><p><img src="/static/docs/studio/images/backend-ports.png" alt="Backend ports" width="285px" class="attempt-right"> </p>

<p>Expand the <strong>Backend ports</strong> section to see a list of running servers,
including their port number and process ID (PID).</p></li>
<li><p>Click the <img src="/static/docs/studio/images/icons/codicon-lock.svg" alt="image of a lock
icon" class="inline-icon"> <strong>Make
public</strong> icon (a lock) to the left of the port number.</p>
<aside class="warning"><strong>Warning:</strong><span> This enables anyone on the internet to access your port while the
workspace is active and until you explicitly turn off public access.</span></aside></li>
<li><p>Click the <img src="/static/docs/studio/images/icons/codicon-copy.svg" alt="image of copy
icon" class="inline-icon"> 
<strong>Copy URL</strong> icon to the right of the port number to copy its
fully-qualified URL.</p></li>
<li><p>You can now reference this URL directly (for example, with a <code translate="no" dir="ltr">fetch</code> call)
from your frontend.</p>
<aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> If your frontend is a web browser, you may need to enable
<a href="https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/CORS">CORS</a> support in
your backend or API server (for example, using the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">cors</code> NPM package for
Node.js apps or <code translate="no" dir="ltr">flask-cors</code> for Python Flask apps).</span></aside></li>
</ol>

<p></section></p>

<p><section class="expandable" expanded id="preview-closed"></p>

<h3 class="showalways" id="preview-closed" data-text="I closed my preview tab. How do I bring it back?" tabindex="-1">I closed my preview tab. How do
I bring it back?</h3>

<p>Open the command palette using <code translate="no" dir="ltr">Ctrl+Shift+P</code> (or <code translate="no" dir="ltr">Cmd-Shift-P</code> on MacOS), then
select <strong><span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span>: Show Android preview</strong> or
<strong><span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span>: Show web preview</strong>.</p>

<p></section></p>

<p><section class="expandable" expanded id="code-oss"></p>

<h3 class="showalways" id="code-oss" data-text="What is Code OSS?" tabindex="-1">What is Code OSS?</h3>

<p>Code-Open Source Software (Code-OSS) is an open-source project that&#39;s the core
layer of VS Code. Code-OSS is available on GitHub under the standard MIT
License, and is where Microsoft develops the VS Code product.</p>

<p></section></p>



<p><section class="expandable" expanded id="ai-training-data"></p>

<h3 class="showalways" id="ai-training-data" data-text="How can I prevent my code completions and Gemini chat prompts from being used as training data?" tabindex="-1">How can I prevent my code
completions and <span class="notranslate">Gemini</span> chat prompts from being used as training
data?</h3>

<p>Your use of <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> is governed by the <a href="https://policies.google.com/terms">Google Terms of
Service</a>.</p>

<p>However, note that your use of generative AI features within
<span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> is governed by the <a href="https://policies.google.com/terms/generative-ai/use-policy">Generative AI Prohibited Use
Policy</a> and the
<a href="https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/terms"><span class=\"notranslate\">Gemini&nbsp;API</span> Additional Terms of
Service</a> (specifically governed by
<a href="https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/terms#unpaid-services"><span class=\"notranslate\">Gemini&nbsp;API</span> Additional Terms of Service: Unpaid
Services</a>).</p>

<p>To block the use of your <em>prompts and responses</em> for model training, do not
use the <span class="notranslate">App Prototyping agent</span>, and do not use assistance from
<span class="notranslate">Gemini</span> within <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span>. To block the use of
your <em>code</em> for model training, turn off
<a href="/docs/studio/set-up-gemini#adjust-code-complete">code completion</a> and
<a href="/docs/studio/set-up-gemini#adjust-code-indexing">code indexing</a>
in your <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> settings.</p>

<p></section></p>

<h2 id="gemini-faq" data-text="Gemini" tabindex="-1"><span class='\"notranslate\"'>Gemini</span></h2>

<p><section class="expandable" expanded id="gemini-key-quota"></p>

<h3 class="showalways" id="gemini-key-quota" data-text="How do I view the request per minute quota for my auto-generated Gemini API key?" tabindex="-1">How do I view the request per
minute quota for my auto-generated Gemini API key?</h3>

<p>You can view the quotas associated with your auto-generated API key on
the <strong>Generative Language API Quotas and System Limits</strong> page in the
<a href="https://console.cloud.google.com//apis/api/generativelanguage.googleapis.com/quotas" class="external"><span class="notranslate">Google Cloud</span> console</a>.</p>

<p></section></p>

<p><section class="expandable" expanded id="migrate-api-key-to-auth-key"></p>

<h3 class="showalways" id="migrate-api-key-to-auth-key" data-text="How do I migrate from an API key to an auth key?" tabindex="-1">How do I migrate from
an API key to an auth key?</h3>

<p>The <span class=\"notranslate\">Gemini&nbsp;Developer&nbsp;API</span> is transitioning from standard API keys to
<a href="https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/api-key#api-keys" class="external">auth keys</a>.
All users must migrate from API keys to auth keys by September 30, 2026 to avoid
service interruption.</p>

<p>As of May 28, 2026, all new <span class=\"notranslate\">Gemini</span> API keys are auth keys by default.
To generate an auth key, follow the instructions to
<a href="/docs/studio/troubleshooting#rotate-gemini-key">change your API key</a>. The new
key will appear as &quot;Gemini Auth key&quot; instead of &quot;Gemini API Key&quot; in the
<a href="https://aistudio.google.com/app/apikey">API Keys</a> page of
<span class=\"notranslate\">Google&nbsp;AI Studio</span>.</p>

<p></section></p>

<p><section class="expandable" expanded id="rotate-gemini-key"></p>

<h3 class="showalways" id="rotate-gemini-key" data-text="How do I rotate my Gemini API key?" tabindex="-1">How do I rotate my Gemini API
key?</h3>

<p>To rotate the Gemini API key used in a <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> project,
generate a new key in <span class=\"notranslate\">Google&nbsp;AI Studio</span> and update it in your
<span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> workspace.</p>

<ol>
<li><p><strong>Generate a new API key</strong></p>

<ol>
<li>Go to the <a href="https://aistudio.google.com/app/apikey"><span class=\"notranslate\">Google&nbsp;AI Studio</span> API keys
page</a>.</li>
<li>Click <strong>Create API key</strong>.</li>
<li>Name your API key and select the correct <span class="notranslate">Google Cloud</span> project. You might
need to import your project if it&#39;s not listed.</li>
<li>Click <strong>Create key</strong>.</li>
<li>Copy the newly generated API key.</li>
</ol></li>
<li><p><strong>Update the API key in your <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> project</strong></p>

<ol>
<li>Open your <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> workspace.</li>
<li>Switch to <img src="/static/docs/studio/images/icons/codicon-code.svg" alt="Code switch icon" class="inline-icon"> 
<strong><span class="notranslate">Code</span></strong> view.</li>
<li>Open the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">.env</code> file (located at <code translate="no" dir="ltr">/home/user/studio/.env</code>).</li>
<li>Replace the old <code translate="no" dir="ltr">GEMINI_API_KEY</code> value with the new key you
copied.</li>
</ol></li>
<li><p><strong>Redeploy or restart (if necessary)</strong></p>

<p>You might need to <a href="/docs/studio/deploy-app">republish your application</a> or
<a href="/docs/studio/troubleshooting#unresponsive-workspace">restart your development server</a>
for the changes to take effect.</p></li>
<li><p><strong>Invalidate the old API key</strong></p>

<ul>
<li><strong>For keys auto-generated by <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span>:</strong>
<ol>
<li>Go to
<a href="https://aistudio.google.com/app/apikey"><span class=\"notranslate\">Google&nbsp;AI Studio</span></a>.</li>
<li>Import the <span class="notranslate">Firebase</span> project of your <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span>
workspace into <span class=\"notranslate\">Google&nbsp;AI Studio</span>.</li>
<li>Locate the auto-generated API key from this project and
delete it.</li>
</ol></li>
<li><strong>For keys generated in <span class=\"notranslate\">Google&nbsp;AI Studio</span> or the
<span class="notranslate">Google Cloud</span> console:</strong>
<ol>
<li>Go to the <a href="https://aistudio.google.com/app/apikey"><span class=\"notranslate\">Google&nbsp;AI Studio</span> API keys
page</a> or the
<a href="https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials"><span class="notranslate">Google Cloud</span> console Credentials
page</a>.</li>
<li>Find the old API key that you replaced and delete it.</li>
</ol></li>
</ul></li>
</ol>

<p></section></p>

<p><section class="expandable" expanded id="max-tokens"></p>

<h3 class="showalways" id="max-tokens" data-text="I received an error about exceeding the maximum number of tokens allowed" tabindex="-1">I received an error about exceeding the
maximum number of tokens allowed</h3>

<p>The amount of data (represented as &quot;tokens&quot;) in your project is larger than the
maximum limit the model can accept. To resolve this error, adjust which files in
your codebase should be hidden from <span class=\"notranslate\">Gemini</span>:</p>

<ol>
<li><p>In your workspace, switch to
<img src="/static/docs/studio/images/icons/codicon-code.svg" alt="Code switch icon" class="inline-icon"> 
<span class="notranslate">Code</span> view.</p></li>
<li><p><a href="/docs/studio/set-up-gemini#exclude-files">Create an <code translate="no" dir="ltr">.aiexclude</code> file</a>.</p></li>
<li><p>Include files or directories <span class=\"notranslate\">Gemini</span> should ignore to reduce the
amount of data in your project. For example, you might want to add <code translate="no" dir="ltr">.next/</code>
and all subdirectories. The path should be relative to the directory that
contains the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">.aiexclude</code> file:</p>
<div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="Text only"><code translate="no" dir="ltr"> .next/
</code></pre></devsite-code></li>
<li><p>Try again to use <span class=\"notranslate\">Gemini</span>. If you still receive an error about
exceeding the
maximum number of tokens, try adding other large files or directories to the
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">.aiexclude</code> file.</p></li>
</ol>

<p></section></p>

<h2 id="prototyper-faqs" data-text="The App Prototyping agent" tabindex="-1">The <span class="notranslate">App Prototyping agent</span></h2>

<p><section class="expandable" expanded id="project-creation-failed"></p>

<h3 class="showalways" id="project-creation-failed" data-text="I was unable to create a project" tabindex="-1">I was unable to create a project</h3>

<p>When provisioning resources like a <span class=\"notranslate\">Gemini&nbsp;API</span> key or deploying to
<span class="notranslate">Firebase App Hosting</span>, a project is automatically provisioned for you, based
on the name of your <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> workspace.</p>

<p>If you receive a &quot;Failed to create a project&quot; error:</p>

<ul>
<li><p>If your Google Account is part of an organization, it&#39;s possible that you
don&#39;t have permission to create <span class="notranslate">Google Cloud</span> projects or that you&#39;ve met
your project quota limit. Contact your administrator for assistance or see
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/resource-manager/docs/creating-managing-projects">Creating and managing
projects</a>.</p></li>
<li><p>If your Google Account is not part of an organization, you may have met your
<span class="notranslate">Google Cloud</span> project quota limit. <a href="https://support.google.com/code/contact/project_quota_increase">Request a quota
increase</a>.</p>

<p>See <a href="https://cloud.google.com/resource-manager/docs/creating-managing-projects#managing_project_quotas">Managing project
quotas</a>
to learn more about project quotas.</p></li>
</ul>

<p>Learn more about Firebase and <span class="notranslate">Google Cloud</span> projects at
<a href="/docs/projects/learn-more">Understand Firebase projects</a>.</p>

<p></section></p>

<p><section class="expandable" expanded id="cloud-billing-failed"></p>

<h3 class="showalways" id="cloud-billing-failed" data-text="Cloud Billing account creation failed" tabindex="-1"><span class="notranslate">Cloud Billing</span> account
creation failed</h3>

<p>When provisioning resources like deploying to
<span class="notranslate">Firebase App Hosting</span>, you can choose or create a <span class="notranslate">Cloud Billing</span> account.</p>

<p>If you receive a &quot;Failed to create a <span class="notranslate">Cloud Billing</span> account&quot; error:</p>

<ul>
<li>Make sure that you have permission to create <span class="notranslate">Cloud Billing</span> accounts.
Check your permissions or contact your administrator for assistance.</li>
</ul>

<p>If you receive a &quot;Too many projects with this billing account&quot; error:</p>

<ul>
<li>You may have met the project limit for your <span class="notranslate">Cloud Billing</span> account.
You can <a href="https://support.google.com/code/contact/billing_quota_increase">request a quota
increase</a>.
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/billing/quotas">Learn more about <span class="notranslate">Cloud Billing</span> account
quotas</a>.</li>
</ul>

<p>Learn more about creating a <span class="notranslate">Cloud Billing</span> account at <a href="https://cloud.google.com/billing/docs/how-to/create-billing-account">Create a new
self-serve billing
account</a>.</p>

<p>If none of these options resolve your issue, contact <a href="https://cloud.google.com/support/docs/get-billing-support"><span class="notranslate">Cloud Billing</span>
support</a>.</p>

<p></section></p>

<p><section class="expandable" expanded id="add-persistence"></p>

<h3 class="showalways" id="add-persistence" data-text="How do I get the App Prototyping agent to automatically add Cloud Firestore and Firebase Authentication to my app?" tabindex="-1">How do I get
the <span class="notranslate">App Prototyping agent</span> to automatically add <span class="notranslate">Cloud Firestore</span> and
<span class="notranslate">Firebase Authentication</span> to my app?</h3>

<p>Prompt the <span class="notranslate">App Prototyping agent</span> to add a database or authentication

while working on an existing app. 
When you ask to add a database or authentication,
the <span class="notranslate">App Prototyping agent</span> asks for confirmation. If you agree,
the <span class="notranslate">App Prototyping agent</span> sets up a Firebase project with the requested
backend services for you.</p>

<p></section></p>



<p><section class="expandable" expanded id="prototyping-agent-fix"></p>

<h3 class="showalways" id="prototyping-agent-fix" data-text="Why doesn't the App Prototyping agent offer to fix my issue?" tabindex="-1">Why doesn't
the <span class="notranslate">App Prototyping agent</span> offer to fix my issue?</h3>

<p>The <span class="notranslate">App Prototyping agent</span> detects Next.js errors and offers to
fix them. If you receive an error and it doesn&#39;t offer to fix it, copy the
issue text and paste it into the chat.</p>

<p>For best results, provide more information about the nature of the issue,
if you have it.</p>

<p>For example, if you see a Firebase error like <code translate="no" dir="ltr">Property access is undefined
on object. for &#39;list&#39; @ L6</code>, which is indicative of an issue with
<span class="notranslate">Cloud Firestore</span> rules, preface the error with, &quot;Can you help me fix this
<span class="notranslate">Cloud Firestore</span> rules issue?&quot;</p>

<p></section></p>

<p><section class="expandable" expanded id="failed-to-publish"></p>

<h3 class="showalways" id="failed-to-publish" data-text='I received a "Failed to publish app" error after publishing' tabindex="-1">I received a "Failed to publish app" error after publishing</h3>

<p>Publishing failures will typically log actionable errors to
<span class="notranslate">Cloud Build</span> logs. To debug and resolve publish failures:</p>

<ol>
<li><p>In the <strong>App Details</strong> page (if minimized, click <strong>Publish</strong> to reveal
it), click <strong>View Details</strong>. This opens <span class="notranslate">App Hosting</span> in the
<span class="notranslate">Firebase</span> console.</p></li>
<li><p>From the <a href="https://console.firebase.google.com/project/_/apphosting"><span class="notranslate">Firebase</span> console
<span class="notranslate">App Hosting</span></a> page, click <strong>View <span class="notranslate">Cloud Build</span> logs</strong>.</p>

<p>This opens the <span class="notranslate">Firebase</span> console where you can see build logs and locate
the error.</p></li>
<li><p>Copy the error and paste it into the <span class="notranslate">App Prototyping agent</span> or
<span class="notranslate">Gemini</span> chat in your workspace and ask
<span class="notranslate">Gemini</span> to fix it.</p></li>
<li><p>To verify the fix, switch to <strong>Code</strong> view, open Terminal, and run <code translate="no" dir="ltr">npm
run build</code>. If you see another error, try again. If you see a
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">FirebaseError</code>, see <a href="/docs/studio/troubleshooting#prototyping-agent-fix">Why doesn&#39;t the <span class="notranslate">App Prototyping agent</span> offer to fix
my issue?</a>.</p></li>
<li><p>When the build is successful, click <code translate="no" dir="ltr">npm run start</code> and open the localhost
link that&#39;s provided and test your app functionality. You can check the
terminal for any runtime errors.</p></li>
<li><p>If all is successful, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">Ctrl-C</code> in Terminal to stop the
production-packaged build running in your workspace, then try the
<span class="notranslate">App Hosting</span> publishing flow again.</p></li>
</ol>

<p></section></p>

<p><section class="expandable" expanded id="no-changes"></p>

<h3 class="showalways" id="no-changes" data-text="I'm unable to make changes using the App Prototyping agent" tabindex="-1">I'm unable to make changes using
the <span class="notranslate">App Prototyping agent</span></h3>

<p>If the <span class="notranslate">App Prototyping agent</span> doesn&#39;t complete requested code changes,
reverts back to the App Blueprint step, or repeatedly returns an error saying
it hit a snag:</p>

<ol>
<li><p><a href="/docs/studio/troubleshooting#unresponsive-workspace">Restart the VM</a>.</p></li>
<li><p>If the problem persists when you reopen your workspace, enter <code translate="no" dir="ltr">/clear</code> in
the <span class="notranslate">App Prototyping agent</span> chat.</p>
<aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> This command erases your
chat history, including the button to <strong>Restore</strong> to a previous point.</span></aside></li>
<li><p>If the problem continues, you can try creating a branch from a previous
version of your app:</p>

<ol>
<li><p>Switch to <img src="/static/docs/studio/images/icons/codicon-code.svg" alt="Code switch icon" class="inline-icon"> 
<span class="notranslate">Code</span> view.</p></li>
<li><p>Open the <strong>Source Control</strong> tab.</p></li>
<li><p>In the Source Control Graph, right-click an earlier version &gt; <strong>Create
Branch</strong>. Enter a name for your branch.</p></li>
<li><p>Return to <span class="notranslate">Prototyper</span> mode. If the agent still
doesn&#39;t respond or returns an error, try branching from an even earlier
version of your app.</p></li>
<li><p>To switch between branches you create (or return to the main branch),
click the branch name located in the bottom-left corner of
<span class="notranslate">Code</span> view and choose the branch you want to use.</p></li>
</ol></li>
</ol>

<p></section></p>

<p><section class="expandable" expanded id="integrations"></p>

<h3 class="showalways" id="integrations" data-text="I'm having trouble prompting the App Prototyping agent to integrate Firebase services." tabindex="-1">I'm having trouble prompting
the <span class="notranslate">App Prototyping agent</span> to integrate Firebase services.</h3>

<p>Here are some common challenges and tips for integrating Firebase services:</p>

<ul>
<li><strong>Configuration file didn&#39;t update</strong>: In your prompt, include the specific
value that you want to update. The values can be found in the
<a href="https://console.firebase.google.com/project/_/settings/general">Project settings</a>
page of the Firebase console. For example, you could prompt: &quot;Update the
measurementId in my config with G-1234567890.&quot;</li>
<li><strong>Authentication doesn&#39;t work when previewing my app</strong>: You may need to
include the preview URL as an authorized domain:
<ol>
<li>In Prototyper mode, click <span class="material-icons" aria-hidden="true" translate="no">open_in_new</span>
<strong>Open in New Window</strong>.</li>
<li>In the new preview window that opens, copy the URL. Note that the URL
should start with <code translate="no" dir="ltr">6000</code>. If it starts with <code translate="no" dir="ltr">9000</code>, update it before
proceeding to the next step.</li>
<li>In the <a href="https://console.firebase.google.com/project/_/authentication/settings">Authentication settings</a>
page of the Firebase console, add the URL you copied in the previous
step to the <strong>Authorized domains</strong>.
Note: This method only enables the default preview shown in
<span class="notranslate">Prototyper</span> mode. The preview within <span class="notranslate">Code</span>
view and the preview pop-out might not allow you to authenticate.</li>
</ol></li>
<li><strong>Firebase Security Rules weren&#39;t created</strong>: <span class="notranslate">Gemini</span> can help
you write security rules, but can&#39;t yet automatically add them to your Firebase
project. You need to copy your Firebase rules into the
<a href="https://console.firebase.google.com/">Firebase console</a> to publish them.</li>
<li><strong>Unexpected interaction with the Firebase MCP server</strong>: If you set up the
<a href="/docs/studio/mcp-servers">Firebase MCP server</a>, you might
encounter unexpected behavior when using <span class="notranslate">Prototyper</span> for
Firebase integrations. If this occurs, switch to <span class="notranslate">Code</span> view
and prompt <span class="notranslate">Gemini</span> to integrate Firebase services.
</section></li>
</ul>

<p><section class="expandable" expanded id="change-favicon"></p>

<h3 class="showalways" id="change-favicon" data-text="How do I change my app's favicon?" tabindex="-1">How do I change my app's favicon?</h3>
<aside class="tip"><strong>Tip:</strong><span> If you&#39;re creating a <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> template, you can set the
workspace icon inside your template for all subsequent uses. Learn more at
<a href="/docs/studio/customize-workspace#custom-icon">Set your workspace icon</a>.</span></aside>
<p>You can change the icon from inside <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span>:</p>

<ol>
<li><p>Switch to <img src="/static/docs/studio/images/icons/codicon-code.svg" alt="Code switch
icon" class="inline-icon"> 
<strong><span class="notranslate">Code</span></strong> view.</p></li>
<li><p>If not already active, click <strong>Explorer</strong> (<code translate="no" dir="ltr">Ctrl+Shift+E</code> or
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">Cmd+Shift+E</code> on Mac) to view all of your files.</p></li>
<li><p>Expand <code translate="no" dir="ltr">src</code>, right-click on the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">app</code> directory, and choose
<strong>Upload...</strong></p></li>
<li><p>When prompted, navigate to and select your <code translate="no" dir="ltr">favicon.ico</code> file from your
local file system.</p></li>
<li><p>When prompted to replace the existing favicon file, click <strong>Replace</strong>.</p></li>
<li><p>Re-deploy your app or clear your browser cache to view the change.</p></li>
</ol>

<p></section></p>
